item.title: Arashiyama Monkey Park: Wild Macaques and a City View — Guide
item.description: The Iwatayama Monkey Park sits on a hilltop above the Arashiyama district, home to a troop of more than a hundred wild Japanese macaques who roam freely across the open summit. Unlike a zoo, here the monkeys are unpenned and the visitors are the ones enclosed: you can buy food and hand it to the macaques through the mesh of a feeding hut, watching them up close while they stay wild and free outside.

item.title: Takasakiyama Monkey Park — Guide
item.description: Takasakiyama Natural Zoological Garden, on a forested mountain overlooking the sea between Beppu and Oita city, is home to large troops of wild Japanese macaques (snow monkeys) that roam free on the mountain. Numbering well over a thousand across two main troops, the monkeys come down to a feeding area where visitors can watch them at close range as they eat, groom, play and interact, revealing the fascinating social hierarchy and family life of the group.
